description:
Bansuri for Dopamine Detox | Music for an Overstimulated Mind | 1.5 Hours

Your mind has been on for too long. Screens, notifications, decisions, sound everywhere — the nervous system is still firing even though the day is meant to be winding down. Not tired enough to sleep. Not clear enough to think. Just overstimulated.

Start here. Ninety minutes of slow bansuri to turn the volume of the world down — gently, without putting you to sleep. A dopamine detox for the evening: less stimulation, more space.

What you'll hear: breathy bamboo flute over a soft drone, unhurried and uncluttered — the feeling of one quiet thing replacing many loud ones.

Best for: end-of-day mental decompression · dopamine fasting / digital detox practice · the hour between work and sleep when the brain refuses to settle · a quiet room and headphones.

🔔 Subscribe to Raga Focus for Indian instrumental music that calms an overstimulated mind, supports dopamine detox, and helps you come back to yourself after a noisy day.
thumbnail_prompt: Pichwai/Kangra miniature painting style, ornate warm-gold patterned border. Evening palette — deep teal and aged-cream parchment, soft amber lantern glow, atmosphere of the world turning quiet. Central figure: a serene, composed musician playing a bansuri (bamboo flute) — body language of relief / settling / letting the noise drop away (NOT slumped-tired, NOT sleepy — quietly restored). IMPORTANT: visually distinct from Sitar Dopamine Reset's thumbnail (different instrument + different overlay text + different posture) so the two videos do not collide in subscriber feed. Overlay text 'OVERSTIMULATED?' in dark-teal serif, large and mobile-readable (1 word + ?, 15 chars, scans under 1 second). Q-hook format (Test 16 cognitive lane winner). Mobile-first: minimal interior clutter, high overlay contrast.
suno_prompt_A: Slow Indian bansuri flute, Raga Yaman — raised teevra Ma, expansive outward-open evening character, the feeling of an overstimulated mind quieting and recalibrating after a noisy dopamine-saturated day, breathy bamboo flute with gentle meend glissando slides and soft murki ornamentation, intimate single-flute presence with no percussion, soft tanpura drone underneath, 432Hz tuning, 55 BPM, mid-low register, warm intimate production with natural breath sounds, seamless loop-friendly texture, like the volume of the world slowly turning down to one quiet voice, restorative and contemplative not drowsy, no tabla, no vocals, no humming, no human voice
suno_prompt_B: Instrumental only, no vocals, no humming, no tabla, no percussion, breathy bansuri bamboo flute, Raga Yaman — teevra Ma expansive evening, soft tanpura drone underneath, 432Hz, 55 BPM, mid-low register, warm intimate single-flute presence, gentle meend and murki ornamentation, natural breath sounds, seamless loop, like an overstimulated mind slowly recalibrating to quiet, restorative not drowsy

production_spec.loop_seam: 10s in / 30s out, Suno extend 3-4x → loop in post to fill 90 min
production_spec.notes: CRITICAL: Bansuri-ONLY (no tabla, no percussion). Slow tempo 55 BPM but NOT drowsy — Alpha 10Hz (relaxed alertness, not sleep). Raga Yaman opens/lifts the overstimulated mind rather than sedating. Breathy intimate flute presence — natural breath sounds OK and desirable (Raga Heal's 449K Bansuri Dopamine had this character). If first Suno clip drifts sleepy/passive, regenerate — the framing is detox/restoration, not sleep. Cannibal-safeguard: do NOT use the same Suno seed/character as Sitar Dopamine Reset — this should sound clearly like a different listening experience (bamboo flute intimate vs sitar plucked spacious).
